ideas.text: An AI that detects when you've been staring at your own face for 4 minutes during a meeting and hides your tile.
A bot that mutes you 0.3 seconds before your dog barks, every time.
An app that detects camera-on social pressure and generates a credible excuse for keeping it off.
A tool that tracks your cumulative Zoom hours per week and automatically cancels calls once you hit a human limit.
An AI that detects when you've joined a meeting on mute and started talking and intervenes before the 8-second mark.
A bot that fixes your lighting before the call starts so you stop looking like you're testifying.
An app that detects when a video call has 22 people and only 2 cameras on and converts it to a phone call.
A tool that cleans your screen share of open tabs before you accidentally reveal something personal.
An AI that detects when you're in your 8th consecutive video call and submits your resignation, jokingly.
A bot that identifies which meeting could have been an email based on post-meeting survey responses no one reads.
An app that converts your gallery view to speaker view the moment someone shares a 90-tab spreadsheet.
A tool that detects when the video freeze makes you look like you're reacting badly to news and unfreezes you.
An AI that schedules a 10-minute break after every 60 minutes of video calls and defends it with force.
A bot that detects when someone joins from a location that is clearly not their listed office and says nothing.
An app that tracks how many meetings you hosted this week versus how many were useful and plots the gap.
A tool that converts 'can everyone see my screen?' into an automated screen share confirmation process.
An AI that detects when you've been on video for 4 hours straight and dims your camera to signal humanity.
A bot that identifies the one person whose audio has been bad in every single meeting for 3 years and sends them a microphone.
An app that blocks anyone from joining a call 10 minutes early and forces them to sit with their thoughts.
A tool that detects when a presenter has lost the room based on collective scrolling patterns and plays an airhorn.
An AI that detects when your video background is more interesting than you and blurs it out of self-interest.
A bot that mutes the person eating chips during a meeting without them realizing it was intentional.
An app that detects when the call could end but nobody wants to be first and triggers a countdown.
A tool that spots when a participant is clearly on mute trying to say something and unmutes them with grace.
An AI that detects Zoom fatigue from face muscle data and gives the presenter 5 minutes to land the plane.
A bot that schedules a 15-minute decompression block after any call involving a difficult stakeholder.
An app that detects when someone joined the wrong meeting link and reroutes them without making it a whole thing.
A tool that counts how many times 'sorry, you go ahead' was said and bills the call for inefficiency.
An AI that calculates the cost of everyone on the call per minute and displays it on the presenter's screen only.
A bot that detects when the host has left the meeting but 4 people are still talking and appoints a new leader.
An app that detects when you're nodding enthusiastically but your eyes haven't moved in 2 minutes.
A tool that prevents anyone from screen sharing a document they haven't opened since last Tuesday.
An AI that detects when you're checking your phone during a video call and closes your camera as a warning.
A bot that converts a 60-minute recurring weekly call into a 3-item Slack update after the fourth consecutive low-engagement session.
An app that detects when the meeting started 7 minutes late because of AV issues and adds those minutes back to your day.
A tool that prevents anyone from ending a sentence with 'does that make sense?' on video calls without a follow-up question.
An AI that detects eye contact with the camera versus eye contact with faces and trains you to look less evasive.
A bot that blocks meetings scheduled at the 30-minute mark of every hour, which is where all the scheduling trauma lives.
An app that detects when a meeting has run over by 10 minutes and stops recording so no evidence exists.
A tool that detects when a breakout room was opened and nobody wanted to go and closes it compassionately.
An AI that converts a 45-minute Zoom debrief about a 30-minute meeting into a two-line summary.
A bot that detects when someone unmutes to say 'great call, everyone' and suggests they use a reaction instead.
An app that plays a soft chime when it's time to end the meeting and a louder one when it's been ignored.
A tool that lets you join a call as a warm beige rectangle when you don't have the energy to be a person today.
An AI that detects when a meeting didn't need to be a meeting 30 seconds after it starts and sends everyone home.
A bot that detects excessive use of meeting platform features like polls and whiteboards and asks if they helped.
An app that mutes the person still talking while everyone else has their jacket on and their cursor near the 'Leave' button.
A tool that detects when someone's internet is buffering and pre-generates their likely next sentence to fill the gap.
An AI that tracks how many times you said 'sorry, my bad' in meetings this week and sends a confidence alert.
A bot that detects when a meeting was called to share information that could have been a PDF and archives both.
An app that blocks video call scheduling after 4pm on Fridays by everyone except people with genuine emergencies.
A tool that asks everyone in the meeting to rate it immediately on a 1-5 scale and shows results to the organizer.
An AI that detects when a recurring weekly call has been going for 2 years without a retrospective and calls an intervention.
A bot that detects when the CEO joined a call and auto-adjusts posture suggestions for every other participant.
